Meeting header:
Date/Time: 2026-11-08 14:30 UTC | Duration: ~58 minutes
Attendees: Maya Patel (Redwood AE), Evan Cho (Redwood SE), Renee Alvarez (Redwood CSM), Daniel Reed (Lyra CTO), Priya Nair (Lyra Head of Platform), Carlos Mendez (Lyra SRE), Samir Gupta (Lyra Security)

Summary:
Quick technical handoff after the region-wide latency episode last week. Focus: root cause recap, immediate hotfix rollout, telemetry gaps (token-level timing and KV cache observability), and compliance/audit asks. Actionable runbook and bench plan agreed.

Topics covered:
- Incident timeline and suspected root cause (KV cache eviction + batching regression)
- Hotfix approach and rollback criteria
- Telemetry debt items (missing token timing, sampling, correlators)
- Compliance: audit logs, KMS rotation, SOC2 artifacts requested by customer security
- Next steps: runbook, bench runs, walkthrough session, timeline for pilot re-verify

Action items (brief): see metadata.

Transcript: (auto transcript; some words may be off)
[00:00] Maya Patel: Alright, thanks everyone for joining. we'll run quick through what happened, what we changed, and then hand off the runbook. Evan, do you want to start with the technical RCA?
[00:21] Evan Cho: Yeah, sure. So, high level — during the 11/04 window we saw token-level latency climb and then periodic evictions in the prefix cache. the KV cash—sorry KV cache— had an eviction storm because the TTL calculation hit a corner case when we had lots of short sequences plus a batch-size increase from a config push. that combination pushed memory pressure on the dedicated pools.
[00:42] Daniel Reed: Can you pause — when you say batch-size increase, was that a Redwood-side change or our config?
[00:48] Evan Cho: Good question. It was a change in Lyra's agent config in the Dedicated routing policy; the app team bumped the intra-request batch target to lower p99 latency for small prompts but unintentionally increased steady-state memory per worker. Redwood's fallback and autoscaler also didn't pre-warm slots fast enough so we had transient queueing and longer tail.
[01:12] Priya Nair: We pushed that change as part of a performance sprint, yeah. We thought smaller prompts would be cheaper with batching but obviously the opposite happened in that traffic mix.
[01:21] Carlos Mendez: To add — we saw a spike in eviction logs around 14:03 UTC and then a downstream cascade: some replica pods started rejecting requests with 503s while the router retried to the fallback model which then saturated.
[01:35] Evan Cho: Exactly. And the KV cache compactor wasn't tuned for that particular eviction pattern — there was a bug in retention calculation where items marked as cold were not reclaimed promptly due to a rounding error in the compaction loop. that's a code-level fix we'll push.
[01:53] Maya Patel: So immediate mitigation path — Evan?
[01:56] Evan Cho: Short-term: 1) revert the batch-size change on Lyra side or cap it in the route config; 2) push a hotfix to the compactor to correct TTL rounding; 3) increase pre-warm buffer on Dedicated pool for the next 24 hours while we validate. The hotfix is small, we can ship it behind a canary in 24–36 hours.
[02:16] Samir Gupta: From security's view, any of these changes affect our compliance posture? We need audit trails and an approval window.
[02:23] Renee Alvarez: We'll provide a one-page change record and a short audit log export showing who pushed what and when — Redwood can supply that as part of the handoff.
[02:29] Samir Gupta: Also need assurance about KMS usage — are we reusing keys or will rotation be impacted?
[02:35] Evan Cho: No key changes planned for the hotfix. It touches runtime compaction only. KMS rotation is independent; we can confirm the rotation cycle does not overlap with the deployment window.
[02:44] Daniel Reed: Ok good. Back to telemetry — Carlos mentioned we didn't have token-timing. we couldn't pinpoint where the p99 spent time.
[02:52] Maya Patel: Right — that's a big one. Evan, what's the delta on traces to get token-level markers?
[02:57] Evan Cho: We can add token-level timing hooks in the runtime to emit coarse markers — it won't be per-token granularity for every request (that'd be expensive) but we can sample 1% of requests and provide detailed spans. That plus adding the request-level correlator in Lyra's tracing should let you correlate a trace to the eviction log entry.
[03:18] Priya Nair: Sampling 1% sounds reasonable; we just need the sample to include heavy and light prompts. How do we control sampling keys?
[03:25] Evan Cho: We'll expose a simple sampling policy: by-customer, by-model, and by-route. Also you can seed by request-id modulus to ensure distribution.
[03:31] Carlos Mendez: If you provide example traces and the schema we can map them to our existing SRE dashboards. we had a blind spot on token timing which made triage slow.
[03:40] Evan Cho: We'll include a sample JSON export and a Kibana/Datadog mapping doc.
[03:44] Maya Patel: Great. Let's run through the rollback criteria and who toggles what. Renee?
[03:48] Renee Alvarez: My plan: Redwood gives you the hotfix image tag + a boolean feature flag to enable compactor changes. Lyra runs the canary on 10% of traffic for 2 hours; if p99 latency improves and there are no eviction logs, we roll to 50%, then 100%. Rollback if error rate > 1% or if p99 doesn't improve by at least 20ms after the canary period.
[04:15] Daniel Reed: That rollback threshold seems fair. who is responsible for the roll? Carlos or Redwood?
[04:20] Maya Patel: It's a joint operation — Lyra ops (Carlos) flips the route cap or feature flag and Redwood will support the Kafka-style rollback if needed. We'll put step-by-step in the runbook.
[04:31] Carlos Mendez: One question about the pre-warm buffer — you suggested bumping it. does that increase cost materially?
[04:37] Evan Cho: Slight uptick, yes. Pre-warm for two extra instances in the pool during peak hour likely adds a small baseline cost; we'll quantify. It should be less than the cost of retries and increased tail latency.
[04:45] Priya Nair: We need the estimated delta because we have a cost committee that reviews any bump.
[04:49] Maya Patel: Evan will provide those estimates in the bench results. Evan, can you include p50/p90/p99 and token-cost delta?
[04:56] Evan Cho: Yep. I'll include experiments with batch-size set to 8/16/32, with and without prewarm scenarios, and the KV cache TTL variants.
[05:05] Daniel Reed: Regarding compliance artifacts — Samir, what do you need from Redwood to sign off?
[05:09] Samir Gupta: At minimum: audit log export for deploys, confirmation that no data left the VPC during incident, and assurance that any debug dumps we request will be redacted per PII guidelines. Also SOC2 artifacts around change management would help.
[05:20] Renee Alvarez: We can package a compliance bundle: deploy audit, redaction checklist, SOC2 summary, and the hotfix review.
[05:25] Samir Gupta: That will be helpful. Also confirm HSM/KMS rotation schedule doesn't collide with our key custodianship plan.
[05:32] Evan Cho: I will double-check and send the schedule.
[05:35] Maya Patel: Ok. Let's talk about telemetry debt — longer term we recommended a small instrumentation sprint. Evan, what are the 3 minimal tickets?
[05:41] Evan Cho: 1) Enable sampled token timing spans; 2) Add eviction event correlator with request-id; 3) Export compacted KV cache metrics (hit/miss, eviction cause) to your metrics backend. Those three will remove the blind spots.
[05:54] Priya Nair: And effort estimate?
[05:56] Evan Cho: Roughly: 3–5 engineer days for the runtime hooks, 2 days to wire exporters, 1 day for docs/tests. So a 1–2 week sprint depending on prioritization.
[06:07] Daniel Reed: Fine. We'll reprioritize a small sprint next cycle.
[06:10] Carlos Mendez: Quick note — when you add token timing, please make the sampling key predictable so we can sync it with our load generator to force-sample certain traces for repro.
[06:19] Evan Cho: Good point. We'll support a request header for forced sampling in debug mode, gated by auth.
[06:24] Maya Patel: Any concerns about the hotfix affecting model outputs or determinism? sometimes compaction touches KV pointers and folks worry about token continuity.
[06:33] Evan Cho: The compactor fix only changes TTL math and reclamation timing; it does not touch KV format. No change to model outputs expected. We'll run A/B on response diff and include a small evaluation prompt set.
[06:47] Priya Nair: Please add that eval set to the runbook so Product and QA can validate.
[06:52] Maya Patel: Will do.
[06:53] (brief cross-talk)
[06:56] Daniel Reed: Another downstream question — when we switch back from fallback model, how do we ensure clients don't see flapping?
[07:03] Evan Cho: We'll use a graceful ramp with request draining. The router will keep routing to warmed replicas and only flip when health checks pass for 5 minutes.
[07:11] Carlos Mendez: Good. Also, can you provide a log-level mapping so our on-call knows which errors are expected vs. critical after the patch?
[07:17] Renee Alvarez: We'll add a triage table in the runbook mapping log messages to severity and suggested action.
[07:22] Samir Gupta: About the audit bundle — we'd like the deploy plan and a signed attestation that no dev keys were used.
[07:29] Maya Patel: Redwood can provide that attestation; we'll include sign-off from our release manager.
[07:34] Priya Nair: Timeline wise — you said 24–36 hours for a canary-ready image — what's the earliest we could start the canary?
[07:40] Evan Cho: If we start build tonight, earliest canary is 36 hours out i.e., 11/09 morning UTC. But we're flexible if you want the 24h path; we need a slot for the release engineer.
[07:49] Daniel Reed: Let's target 11/09 10:00 UTC for the canary; Carlos will own toggling.
[07:55] Carlos Mendez: I have the window free.
[07:57] Maya Patel: Great. We'll send calendar invite after.
[07:59] (short pause)
[08:02] Evan Cho: One last item — cost estimate. Prewarm + additional buffer vs retries: I'll send a 7-day cost simulation with traffic profile you provided.
[08:11] Daniel Reed: Fine.
[08:13] Maya Patel: Anything else from Lyra?
[08:15] Priya Nair: We just want the runbook and sample traces. After the canary we expect a 48h observation window, then a signoff.
[08:23] Maya Patel: Sounds good. To recap next steps — Maya to upload runbook and hotfix link; Evan to run micro-bench and telemetry plan; Carlos to run canary on 11/09 10:00 UTC; Samir to review compliance bundle. We'll close once the 48-hour observation completes.
[08:45] Daniel Reed: Thank you all. Appreciate the quick turnaround.
[08:49] Renee Alvarez: Thanks, we'll follow up with the bundle and invite.
[08:52] (meeting ends)
